authors: Claude Code session (data request for the fall-degree paper)

links.prior_data: crypto-autoresearcher:analysis/semaev-m2-last-fall-degree/results/ (93 m=2 instances, 12 chain instances, 13 checked certificates)

question: For the binary Weil descent of Semaev's S_3 (m=2, k=ceil(n/2)), (a) does the certified bound d_F >= 5 hold on every random-subspace instance and on Semaev's polynomial subspace from n=45 upward, for n up to 51; and (b) does the last fall degree reach 6 on any instance where W_5 is computable (n=33-37)?

claims.text: For each new instance with 1 not in W_4(F) by closure A, an independent certificate check (cert_check.py, own descent) accepts 1 not in W_4(F), so d_F >= 5 on that instance.
For each instance already certified d_F >= 5 at n=33-37 (T33a/b, R35a/b, U35a/b, R37a/b) the degree-5 closure decides 1 in W_5 (d_F = 5) or 1 not in W_5 (d_F >= 6, certified as in C1).
The existing uncertified d_F >= 5 instances R39a, R39b, C21a, C21b receive checked certificates, or the record says which check failed.
Per (family, n) cell, the fraction of instances with d_F >= 5 is reported with a Clopper-Pearson interval; no trend in n is claimed from these counts.

hypotheses.statement: On random subspaces the last fall degree stays >= 5 for every n in 39-51.
hypotheses.mechanism: Random subspaces at n >= 35 already defeat degree 4 (Theorem 6.11); the degree-4 closure stalls with codim W_4 growing with n (4,888 at n=33 to 12,742 at n=45).

predictions.minimum_effect: every R instance at n=41-51 has 1 not in W_4

data_seen.measured: R: 2x>=5 at n=35,37,39; polynomial: 4 at n<=43, >=5 at n=45

hypotheses.statement: Some instance at n=33-37 has d_F >= 6.
hypotheses.mechanism: R35a is exactly 5 by branching; whether any other certified instance needs degree 6 is unknown. A 6 would be the first evidence that d_F grows past 5 at fixed m=2.

predictions.minimum_effect: at least one of the 8 certified n=33-37 instances has 1 not in W_5

data_seen.measured: W_4 dims and codim only; no W_5 computed

arms.description: lfdclose2 (M4RI dense echelon, degree-descending colex order) computes W_D for D=4 (n=37-51) and D=5 (n=33-37); writes the quotient map as a certificate when 1 is not in W_D.
cert_check.py rebuilds the equations from the curve parameters with its own descent and checks the certificate (Proposition 1.5); independent of closureA's code path.
closureA rerun on a 10% subset with OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 instead of 8: W_D dimensions must be identical (determinism floor).
Instances with recorded 1 in W_4 (P35a, P41a, S40a, U33a): closureA must report 1 in W_4 again.
Satisfiable instances (Boolean solutions planted by drawing the target as a sum of two base points), one per n: 1 can never lie in W_D, so a refutation here is an instrument fault.

positive.expected_detection: 1 in W_4 on all 4 instances, with W_4 dimensions equal to the recorded ones

null_population.description: satisfiable descent systems: 1 never lies in W_D because a Boolean solution exists
null_population.generator: gen2.py with the target drawn as P1+P2, P_i in the factor base (planted decomposition)
null_population.why_n: one per n in 33-51: any single refutation is an instrument fault, so one per size suffices

factors.name: curve_and_target
factors.how: drawn by gen2.py from seeds derived from the protocol hash (protocol_hash_sha256), independent of arm

factors.name: subspace_basis
factors.how: R: uniform random k-dim F_2-subspace from the same seed; P: <1,t,...,t^{k-1}>

factors.name: z_mode
factors.how: z on the curve, as in instances.json families P and R

factors.name: binary
factors.how: one lfdclose2 build, sha256 recorded per row; M4RI 20200125

factors.name: host
factors.how: instance type, CPU model, kernel recorded per row; affects wall time only

factors.name: implementation
factors.how: closureA (C, M4RI, colex order) and certcheck (Python integers, own descent) both run on every certified instance

factors.name: spot_preemption
factors.how: attempts recorded; an interrupted closure is rerun from scratch

comparisons.threshold: certcheck accepts closureA's certificate (exact agreement on 1 not in W_D)

randomization.arm_order_reason: exact computation: certcheck consumes closureA's certificate, so it must follow it; no clock is a primary metric

seed_derivation.note: curve, target and subspace seeds per (n, family, index) from `experiment_protocol.py seeds --all` after freeze

instance_sampling.rule: per cell: R 3 instances at n=41,43,45,47,49,51; P 2 instances at n=37,39,47,49,51; existing named instances for C2 and C3; an instance whose target decomposes (Boolean solution exists) is moved to the negative-control set and redrawn, and the redraw is reported

blinding.how: not masked: outcomes are exact membership tests checked by an independent program

power.note: every claim is an exact per-instance computation; C4's intervals are descriptive (3 instances per R cell give a Clopper-Pearson lower bound of 0.29 at 3/3)

preflight_runtime.measured_on: recorded closures: D=4 at n=45 took 1850.7 s (P45a) and ~6000 s with certificate output; D=5 at n=35 is estimated from column count (about 0.38M columns, ~18 GB dense), not measured

primary.name: last fall degree
primary.definition: least D with 1 in W_D(F); reported as '>= D+1' when 1 not in W_D and the certificate checks

primary.name: certified codimension
primary.definition: cert_check.py's lower bound on codim W_D(F)

primary.name: share of instances with d_F >= 5
primary.definition: instances with checked 1 not in W_4 over admissible instances in the cell

secondary.name: closure dimensions
secondary.definition: dim W_D cap B_{<=d} for d=0..D

secondary.name: closure columns
secondary.definition: columns of the degree-D closure matrix

secondary.name: closure wall time
secondary.definition: process start to closure verdict, host recorded

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: run every listed cell once; D=5 closures only on the 8 named instances
a closure that exceeds its memory or 48 h limit is recorded as censored (no verdict) and not retried beyond the infrastructure limit
any positive-control miss or negative-control refutation stops the study: the instrument is faulty

invalidation_rules: a d_F >= D+1 row without an accepted certificate is reported as 'closure A only' and does not enter C1 or C2
an A/A mismatch in any W_D dimension invalidates every row from that binary
wall times are descriptive only (no isolation)

decision_rule.text: C1/C3: per instance, certified when certcheck accepts. C2: d_F = 5 if 1 in W_5, d_F >= 6 if 1 not in W_5 and the degree-5 certificate checks. P1 holds if every admissible R instance at n=41-51 is certified >= 5; P2 holds if any named instance is certified >= 6.
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: d_F per instance and certified codimension

graphs: d_F by n and family, certified vs closure-only

inadmissible: redrawing an instance because its d_F is inconvenient (only decomposable targets are redrawn, and every redraw is reported)
calling d_F >= 6 without an accepted degree-5 certificate
reading the cell fractions as a growth law in n

literature.claim: last fall degree framework and the closure W_D

literature.claim: F4 D_reg = 5 for m=2, n=37-48 (photographed page 236, 2026-10-29)
